strings, so I wrote `string`.
- **"Not mutated":** line 21 returns a new object built with spread syntax, and the tabs list comes from `.filter`, which makes a new array. The input is never written to.
- **`key`:** it's a string because `openTab` builds it as `` `t${state.next}` `` and the test calls `closeTab(s, "t2")`.
- **Unknown key:** `filter((tab) => tab.key !== key)` keeps every tab, so you still get a new state object with the same tabs.
- **Return value:** it's always a new object with the same shape as `state`. `next` is copied over unchanged by the spread and `tabs` is the filtered array. There are no early returns and no null or undefined returns.
- **Errors:** the function only throws a `TypeError` if `state` or `state.tabs` is missing or invalid. That only happens with bad input, so I left out a `@throws` tag to keep the comment short.

**Full `git diff`:**
```diff
diff --git a/src/tabs/tab-keys.mjs b/src/tabs/tab-keys.mjs
index 830a094..6ac0aef 100644
--- a/src/tabs/tab-keys.mjs
+++ b/src/tabs/tab-keys.mjs
@@ -9,6 +9,14 @@ export function openTab(state, title) {
   return { next: state.next + 1, tabs: [...state.tabs, { key, title }] };
 }
 
+/**
+ * Removes the tab with the given key. The other tabs keep their keys and `next` is unchanged,
+ * so closing `t2` of `t1,t2,t3` leaves `t1,t3` (see §stable-tab-keys in PRECEDENT.md).
+ *
+ * @param {{ next: number, tabs: { key: string, title: string }[] }} state - Tab strip state; not mutated.
+ * @param {string} key - Key of the tab to close, e.g. `"t2"`. An unknown key removes nothing.
+ * @returns {{ next: number, tabs: { key: string, title: string }[] }} A new state object without that tab.
+ */
 export function closeTab(state, key) {
   return { ...state, tabs: state.tabs.filter((tab) => tab.key !== key) };
 }
```
`git status` shows only `M src/tabs/tab-keys.mjs`.

**Tests:** `npm test` (`node --test`) passed all 3 tests, including "close keeps keys". The project has no lint script, so I didn't run one.
